content:
Let each square have side length \(1\), and place the origin at the lower-left corner.

### Square I
The diagonal has equation \(y=1-x\), while the segment from the lower-left corner to the top midpoint has equation \(y=2x\). Their intersection satisfies
\[
1-x=2x,
\]
so \(x=\frac13\), \(y=\frac23\).

Thus the shaded triangle has base \(1\) and height \(\frac23\):
\[
S_I=\frac12(1)\left(\frac23\right)=\frac13.
\]

### Square II
The diagonal is again \(y=1-x\), while the segment from the lower-left corner to the right midpoint is \(y=\frac{x}{2}\). Hence
\[
1-x=\frac{x}{2},
\]
giving \(x=\frac23\), \(y=\frac13\). Therefore,
\[
S_{II}=\frac12(1)\left(\frac13\right)=\frac16.
\]

### Square III
The two segments have equations
\[
y=1-2x
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
y=\frac{x}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
1-2x=\frac{x}{2},
\]
so \(x=\frac25\), \(y=\frac15\). The shaded triangle has base \(\frac12\) and height \(\frac15\), giving
\[
S_{III}=\frac12\left(\frac12\right)\left(\frac15\right)=\frac1{20}.
\]

Since
\[
\frac1{20}<\frac16<\frac13,
\]
the comparison is
\[
\boxed{\text{D: }S_{III}<S_{II}<S_I}.
\]
